A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiMA and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite extensive expansion and reorganization in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original protein-generation experiments on SwissProt and AFDBv4-90, including baseline comparisons, architectural ablations, and biological annotation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation experiments and adds encoder comparisons, joint sequence-structure generation, and conditional-design results, including those in Tables 7 and 10–14.

M1.justification: v2 extends the unconditional pipeline with classifier guidance, family-label conditioning, an infilling adapter, and motif/fold conditioning components. CHEAP integration enables joint sequence and backbone outputs. The decoder description also changes from two linear layers plus an activation to one linear layer. The core denoiser, diffusion objective, self-conditioning, and length-sampling approach remain.

E1.justification: SwissProt and AFDBv4-90 remain, but v2 adds family-conditioned generation across eight families, sequence infilling, functional-motif scaffolding, joint sequence-structure generation, and fold-conditioned design. New coverage includes the 24-problem scaffolding benchmark and CATH S40, TIM-barrel, and NTF2 fold evaluations.

E2.justification: The SwissProt comparison retains nanoGPT, EvoDiff-OADM, SeqDesign, and ProteinGAN while adding Walk-Jump, RITA, D3PM, DFM, and DPLM (v2 Tables 2 and 6). Separate pretrained and conditional comparisons add methods including ProtGPT2, ProGen2, ProLLAMA, RFDiffusion, and Multiflow. The SUPERFAMILY comparison also changes comparator membership, prominently introducing DPLM.

E3.justification: The reported matched model budget changes from 33M to 35M. v2 describes held-out distributional evaluation where v1 described training-data references, replaces SeqD/30%-identity clustering with repetition and revised clustering measures, and adds novelty, ProGen perplexity, and structural distribution metrics. New tasks introduce masking, success thresholds, and best-of-10 or 100-design protocols. These are reported settings, not proof that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds decoder-finetuning and flow-matching ablations, a generation-step sensitivity study, and encoder-capacity/compression analyses. It extends the existing length-masking analysis with quantitative quality results rather than introducing that question anew. Biological analyses gain domain-overlap comparisons, and conditional experiments add structural case studies and failure observations (Appendices E–F).

E5.justification: The existing out-of-distribution pLDDT plus/minus summaries and secondary-structure dispersion plot are retained. Neither version documents repeated-training seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new multiple-design attempts specify sampling and selection protocols rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The SwissProt DiMA row changes from pLDDT 80.8 and FPD 0.41 in v1 Table 1 to 83.3 and FD-seq 0.34 in v2 Tables 5–6. Changed model descriptions prevent treating this as a controlled same-setting gain. Substantial new results include 42.2% infilling success versus DPLM's 40.0%, 19/24 scaffolding problems solved, and the fold-conditioned results in Table 14.

T1.justification: Appendix B removes the SeqD definitions and introduces mathematical definitions for subsequence repetition, cluster-density measures, and alignment-based novelty. These are limited changes to evaluation mathematics. The central diffusion loss and noise-schedule equations remain equivalent, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v1 presents superior unconditional generation using ESM-2 and treats conditional generation as future work. v2 claims generality across multiple encoder families, demonstrated conditional and backbone-generation capabilities, and performance comparable to multibillion-parameter models using a 35M-parameter denoiser. This substantially broadens the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of encoder quality/diversity tradeoffs, DPLM repetition and domain-length behavior, and the advantage of richer fold-conditioning information. It explicitly qualifies pLDDT in intrinsically disordered regions and discusses infilling failures. Conversely, v1's dedicated discussion of monomer/length restrictions and unexplored scalability is removed, although dataset length filters remain documented.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses batch size, learning rate, gradient clipping, warmup, EMA, four A100 80GB GPUs, and approximately ten days per training session (Appendix C.2). Conditional experiments add adapter specifications, training budgets, sampling settings, and baseline initialization details. These are documentation additions; v1's direct DiMA code-access link is omitted without a replacement.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around protein flow models, DPLM/DPLM2, Walk-Jump, CHEAP, SaProt, and other recent approaches. Its introduction explicitly distinguishes earlier continuous protein models by restricted representations or conditional focus, including newly cited Pro-LDM. This changes the research positioning beyond merely relocating related work to Appendix D.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Numbered method subsections become compact thematic paragraphs, experiments are reorganized around components, representations, and conditional applications, and much metric exposition and related work move to the appendices. v2 also adds an appendix contents page and changes 'embeddings' to 'encodings' in the title.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the original combined results presentation with compact main-text summaries and expanded, metric-grouped appendix tables. It adds model-size comparisons, family radar charts, conditional structural examples, and a domain-overlap Venn diagram; noise and length plots are redrawn. The original pipeline overview disappears, while UMAP, architecture, disorder, and secondary-structure graphics are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for encoder generality and conditional utility that v1 left untested. The targeted ablations, novelty/diversity assessments, conditional benchmarks, and training disclosures make the framework's capabilities more assessable and reproducible. These gains outweigh the omitted code link and explicit limitations discussion, although reporting inconsistencies reduce confidence in particular comparisons—for example, ESMc CD0.5 is 0.963 in Table 3 but 0.863 in Table 7.
